intro: A converter that turns a Julian date (from the old calendar) into a Gregorian date (today's calendar), and back, for the place you pick. It flags dates that never existed there, like 13 October 1582 in Rome. Made for family historians and anyone reading old letters: a sample is loaded, so change the day or place, or try a famous date.
title: Historical Date Converter
tagline: Convert old dates to today's calendar, find the days a place skipped, and check every step.
description: Converts a date between the Julian and Gregorian calendars using the switch day of the place you choose, and flags dates that never existed there. It shows the weekday and every step of the working, and runs entirely in your browser.

sources.title: The Gregorian Calendar Adopted in England
When Did the Gregorian Calendar Start in Each Country? (Family Tree Magazine)
Give us our eleven days!: calendar reform in eighteenth century England

makingOf: The converter does its own whole-number day arithmetic for both calendars and never uses the browser's date tools, which cannot hold dates such as 29 February 1700. Each place has one switch day, taken from the sources listed here; rows that rest only on search results are marked with their date. Everything is computed in your browser, and a self-test in the page re-checks the known answers whenever you ask.
